title: The ethical debate about the gig economy: A review and critical analysis
abstract: The gig economy is a phenomenon that is rapidly expanding, redefining the nature of work. This article provides a clear and systematic analysis of the main ethical challenges caused by the gig economy. Following a brief overview, we map the key ethical problems it gives rise to, as discussed in the relevant literature, onto three categories: the new organisation of work, the new nature of work, and the new status of workers. We then evaluate a recent EU initiative and argue that ethical concerns relating to algorithmic control and the disconnectedness faced by gig workers require further deliberation and policy response.

title: Unpacking the gig economy: key enablers and barriers for gig work - a systematic review and future research directions
abstract: This study systematically reviews and synthesizes existing literature on gig work to identify its key enablers and barriers. With the rise of algorithmically managed digital platforms, gig work faces unique challenges. Using Bronfenbrenner's Ecological Systems framework, this study systematically reviews 83 research articles. The review identifies enablers and barriers, and gaps in current research, particularly on the long-term impacts of gig work. The review aims to offer insights and guide future research on this evolving labour market segment.

title: The organisation and experience of work in the gig economy
abstract: The gig economy has captured public and policy interest and is growing as an area of academic inquiry, prompting debate about the future of work, labour regulation, and job quality. This introductory article positions a special issue within a comprehensive literature review of existing scholarship on the gig economy. It delineates avenues for further research regarding conditions for gig workers, the impact of gig work, and information technology and gig work.

title: A Systematic Literature Review of the Gig Economy: Insights into Worker Experiences, Policy Implications, and the Impact of Digitalization
abstract: With adherence to PRISMA guidelines, this systematic literature review synthesizes results from 31 studies retrieved from Scopus and Web of Science. It explores three areas: worker well-being, legal and policy aspects, and how digitalization reshapes job structures. The review highlights the importance of targeted interventions to balance flexibility with worker protections, offering a framework that can guide future research and policymaking in the developing gig economy.
venue: Int. J. Research and Innovation in Social Science

title: Socio-technical issues in the platform-mediated gig economy: A systematic literature review (ARIST paper)
abstract: Because the platform-mediated gig economy is a relatively new phenomenon, studies have produced a range of findings. This systematic literature review provides a snapshot of socio-technical issues raised in the last 12 years. Based on 515 papers, 132 were coded. Three socio-technical themes were identified: the digital workplace, algorithmic management, and ethical design. The results draw attention to understudied yet critically important socio-technical issues that suggest opportunities for future research directions.

title: Systematic Literature Review on Gig Economy: Power Dynamics, Worker Autonomy, and the Role of Social Networks
abstract: This study explores the dynamics of collective agency among gig workers. Using a systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis of 59 articles, it examines power dynamics, worker autonomy, and social networks, and how algorithmic management affects gig workers' agency. It proposes directions for future research to address power imbalances and enhance worker empowerment.

title: Work in the platform economy: a systematic literature review
abstract: This study reviews research focusing on the gig economy to explore alternative work arrangements. A systematic literature review of 258 studies following SPAR-4-SLR protocols. Our analysis shows most existing literature is based on gig service providers; there is little research focusing on gig goods providers, gig data providers, and agency gig workers. We aim to enhance understanding of existing literature and highlight underexplored areas for future research.

title: Physical and psychological hazards in the gig economy system: A systematic review
abstract: Gig economy platforms expose workers to a raft of safety hazards and research beyond individual contributing factors is limited. This systematic review addresses this limitation using Rasmussen's Risk Management Framework to map hazards across the gig work system. Following PRISMA-P, 34 articles were included. This study is the first to provide a holistic representation of the hazards across the gig economy system, a critical step in understanding the systemic nature of factors contributing to safety outcomes.

title: Exploring the Work Perceptions and Experiences of Gig Workers Globally: A Scoping Review
abstract: This scoping review mapped global evidence on gig workers' experiences between 2018 and 2024, following PRISMA-ScR guidelines. From 1986 records, 26 met inclusion criteria. Three themes emerged: freedom and flexibility; variation across demographic and geographic contexts; and precarity. The findings illustrate how autonomy and vulnerability coexist, highlighting the importance of policies that promote safe, stable and dignified work.

title: Exposure to Psychosocial Risk Factors in the Gig Economy: A Systematic Review
abstract: The gig economy refers to a market system in which companies hire workers to perform short assignments mediated through online platforms. In addition to specific hazards, there are psychosocial risks related to the way gig work is organised. The aim of this review is to provide a comprehensive overview of these risks, identifying research gaps and strategies to address them.

title: The Gig Economy: Disruption, Innovation, and Economic Evolution
abstract: This review paper synthesizes the existing research landscape to elucidate the multifaceted dimensions of the gig economy phenomenon. Through a comprehensive analysis it navigates the disruptive forces reshaping traditional employment, examines drivers behind gig work, explores innovative aspects, and critically evaluates precarious conditions. It underscores the need for nuanced policy frameworks that balance innovation with social protection.

title: Gig Economy's Impact On Workforce Dynamics And Economic Resilience
abstract: This review paper examines the multifaceted impact of the gig economy on workforce dynamics and economic resilience. Through a comprehensive analysis of existing literature, this study seeks to illuminate the complex interplay between gig work, traditional employment, and broader economic structures. It underscores the need for nuanced policy responses that balance flexibility with worker well-being.

title: The influence of digital platforms on gig workers: A systematic literature review
abstract: Despite this issue's growing importance, no systematic literature review has explicitly examined the influence of digital platforms on gig workers. This study fills this gap by conducting a comprehensive review of 18 articles published between 2019 and 2023 using PRISMA. Thematic analysis revealed 12 key themes. As the gig economy expands globally, researchers, platforms, and policymakers must work together to ensure benefits are shared more equitably.
authors: Alauddin, F. D. A. et al.

title: Algorithmic management in the gig economy: A systematic review and research integration
abstract: There has been an increase in scholarship related to algorithmic management across scientific domains. However, this literature is fragmented with scholars disagreeing on the conceptualization and measurement of AM, and a lack of consensus on its dimensions. To address these issues, we systematically reviewed the literature using NLP-based topic modeling. We provide a comprehensive definition of AM and a roadmap for future research using an organizational behavior lens.

title: Connecting the Dots in Digital Labor Marketplace: A Bibliometric Review of Global Gig Dynamics
abstract: This study addressed the imperative need to comprehend and contextualize gig dynamics. It endeavors a comprehensive bibliometric review, shedding light on trends shaping the dynamics using the Dimensions database. Thematic analysis emphasized emerging trends such as digital platform work, regulatory efficiencies, and socioeconomics. This review informs future research agendas and fosters a deeper understanding.
venue: Int. J. Entrepreneurship, Business and Creative Economy

title: New tech, old exploitation: Gig economy, algorithmic control and migrant labour
abstract: Digital platforms are the newest technological wave reshaping the labour landscape. This review highlights two main themes that have emerged within the on-demand gig economy in the current literature: mythical autonomy and algorithmic control, and misclassification of labour and the complexity of migrant workers. Finally, this review calls for further research into the inside/outside dichotomy of migrant labour and their experiences of labour exploitation.

title: Digital labour markets in the platform economy: mapping the political challenges of crowd work and gig work
abstract: This study takes a closer look at platform-based digital business models and their implications. It focusses on the socio-politically most contested ones, digital labour platforms. These platforms rely on a workforce of independent contractors who work for low wages and without social security. The study maps the political challenges of crowd work and gig work.

title: Workers organizing in the platform economy: Local forms and global trends of collective action
abstract: Distinctive features of on-demand work platforms made it theoretically improbable for workers to organize. However, collective actions of platform workers surged. Through a literature review focused on Europe, Latin America, North America and Asia, this article shows that workers struggle globally to build a collective actor, through an original combination of new and old forms of protest.
authors: Rafelis de Broves, O. & Murgia, A.

title: Mapping the Gig Economy: A Systematic Review and Bibliometric Analysis of Gig Worker Research
abstract: This study aims to map and analyze research trends on gig workers using the bibliometric method with a PRISMA flow diagram. 523 Scopus publications from 2020 to 2025 were analyzed to identify publication patterns and dominant keywords. This study provides a comprehensive overview that can be used by researchers to identify research gaps and formulate relevant research questions.

title: Gig economy insights: key trends, influencers and research directions
abstract: This study aims to conduct a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of the gig economy, focusing on its evolving landscape, key contributors and significant themes. Using 657 Scopus publications, it reveals patterns of publications and emerging themes including labour regulation, algorithmic management and digital platforms. This study maps the intellectual landscape and offers recommendations concerning areas for future research.
authors: Kamarul Zaman, N. J. F. et al.

title: Quantifying the gig economy's evolution: A bibliometric exploration of historical patterns and future projections
abstract: This paper provides an overview of gig economy literature up to June 2025, identifying key themes and future research directions. Using multiple bibliometric techniques, it examines major trends. Results reveal an expanding conceptual and thematic landscape, demonstrating the role of bibliometric analysis in anticipating research directions and informing future inquiry.

title: Bibliometric Analysis of Gig Economy
abstract: This article presents a systematic review of the literature associated with a bibliometric analysis of the global perspective of the gig economy. The study aims to present the analysis of published articles that explore the gig economy. From 2297 documents, 686 publications were selected for bibliometric analysis. The results highlight publication trends, top contributing authors and countries, most cited articles, and keywords.

title: Analysing the evolution and patterns of the gig economy: a bibliometric examination of growth and trends
abstract: This article examines global academic research and provides an overview of the gig economy, offering insights into the evolution of research trends, key themes, and collaborative dynamics. Using bibliometric analysis of 341 Scopus documents, our findings reveal a significant increase in publication research and identify three cluster themes. The article sheds light on the current state and potential future directions.

title: Comprehending the research on the gig economy: a bibliometric approach
abstract: This paper aims to quantitatively explore the trends and patterns of the existing literature in the gig economy. Using 1707 documents from Scopus and Web of Science, bibliometric analysis was performed. It highlights the most prolific authors and emerging themes such as labor, technology, management and precarity. By mapping thematic clusters and identifying trending topics, it provides a perspective on the field's development and emerging areas of focus.

title: Entrepreneurship and the gig economy: A bibliometric analysis
abstract: There is a lack of a global picture depicting the scientific structure of knowledge regarding the gig economy and entrepreneurship. This paper presents a conceptual, intellectual, and social bibliometric overview of 345 articles. Five main clusters emerged. The main themes deal with sharing, gig, and platform economy, digitalization, and platforms. Gig workers are key for developing strategies through entrepreneurship.

title: The Rise of The Gig Economy and Its Impact on HRM Research: a Dynamic Bibliometric Analysis
abstract: This study conducts a dynamic bibliometric analysis of 2695 articles to map the evolution and research trends at the intersection of the gig economy and HRM. Keyword co-occurrence reveals consolidation around three major, yet poorly integrated, thematic clusters. Bibliographic coupling confirms fragmentation within the intellectual community. These findings underscore the need for a future research agenda that is more integrative across paradigms.

title: Bibliometric Analysis on the Emergence of the Gig Economy
abstract: The research aims to enhance the understanding of the gig economy through a comprehensive bibliometric analysis. Using co-citation and co-occurrence techniques, this study identifies key articles, prominent topics, and emerging trends. The study highlights three primary research clusters and key emerging topics. Future research should delve deeper into these dimensions to maximize opportunities while addressing challenges.

title: Unveiling Insights of Gig Economy through a Bibliometric Analysis
abstract: This study explores the scholarly landscape surrounding gig work, focusing on trends, key themes, and influential contributions. 3828 WoS articles were analysed using bibliometric analysis. The results illuminate the interdisciplinary nature of gig work research. The paper pinpoints emerging topics and gaps in the existing literature, offering valuable insights for future research endeavours.

title: A Glance Into The World Of Gig Economy: A Review & Bibliometric Analysis
abstract: Comprehensive review of the existing literature has been done to analyze the theoretical concepts and current developments in Gig Economy. 526 WoS papers were analyzed by a two-tier method combining bibliometric analysis and systematic literature review. This study highlights future research themes by identifying knowledge gaps based on literature review.

title: Gig economy and sustainable development: bibliometric analysis and identification of future research directions
abstract: The aim of this article is to identify the most common fields of study undertaken by researchers in papers covering the gig economy and sustainable development. Using a structured literature review method, 48 Scopus studies were selected. The analyses showed sustainable development is addressed in the context of the gig economy, a relatively new research area. Attention is drawn to future research directions on green jobs.
venue: Silesian Univ. of Technology Org. and Mgmt Series

title: Transformative dynamics of the gig economy: Technological impacts, worker well-being and global research trends
abstract: Using the Scopus database, a literature analysis on the gig economy was conducted with 1624 documents narrowed to 549. This study highlights the evolving nature of non-traditional, online-platform-driven employment, exploring challenges, ethical issues, and career development. For sustainable growth, further research should explore the platform economy, gig employment, and worker well-being.

title: A Decade of Gig Economy Research (2014-2025): A Bibliometric and Scientific Mapping of Digital Labor Scholarship
abstract: This study investigates how the academic discourse on the gig economy has evolved between 2014 and June 2025. Despite growing scholarly attention, the literature remains conceptually fragmented and lacks conceptual clarity and methodological coherence. Drawing on 1303 Scopus publications, the study uncovers structural foundations and dynamic shifts, identifies conceptual blind spots, and offers strategic insights for future research.
venue: J. Information System and Technology Management

title: Understanding the Landscape of Gig Workers' Well-Being: A Bibliometric Analysis
abstract: Given the inherently precarious nature of gig work, this shift has brought to light the importance of prioritizing gig workers' well-being. This study aims to analyze peer-reviewed literature to assess the current understanding of gig workers' well-being and identify research gaps. 862 articles were analyzed. By highlighting geographical disparities, the study provides valuable insights to guide future research directions.

title: Mapping research on well-being of gig workers: A bibliometric analysis
abstract: This study aims to assess the existing body of research on the well-being of gig workers, with the goal of identifying significant aspects, emerging patterns, and potential topics for future research. 478 documents were analyzed. The findings suggest that the well-being of gig workers has recently received attention; nevertheless, a noticeable gap exists across several dimensions, underscoring the need for future scholarly enquiry.

title: Exploring the emerging research themes on algorithmic management: a bibliometric analysis approach
abstract: The research aims to map and quantify the academic literature on algorithmic management from a bibliometric viewpoint and present an analysis of future research development trends. 715 Scopus articles were extracted. The analysis revealed a substantial rise in publications from 2019 onwards. Keyword co-occurrence revealed five themes and offered direction for further investigation.

title: Shaping the gig economy: insights into management, technology, and workforce dynamics
abstract: This study offers a bibliometric analysis of gig economy research, drawing from 84 Scopus articles to uncover key themes such as worker vulnerability, regulatory frameworks, and digital platforms. Findings highlight the multidisciplinary nature; gaps persist in exploring worker well-being, regulatory efficacy, and sustainable practices. Future research should address underexplored areas such as mental health and job sustainability.
venue: Int. J. Accounting and Economics Studies

title: Clarifying the sharing, gig, and on-demand economies and their implications for entrepreneurship: A systematic literature review
abstract: The article aims to develop conceptual clarity around three distinct terms emanating from the platform economy. We applied aggregative systematic review methodology to clarify and operationalise the differences among the on-demand, gig, and sharing economies. We argue that the lack of consistent definitions has resulted in several misconceptions and reduced potential progress with further studies.

title: A Typology of Crowdwork Platforms
abstract: Despite growing interest in the gig economy, the area is replete with different terminology, definitional constructs and contested claims about the ensuing transformation of work. The aim of this positional piece is to provide a timely review and classification of crowdwork. A typology is developed to map the complexity of this emerging terrain. Rather than side-tracking into debates as to what exactly constitutes crowdwork, the purpose is to highlight commonalities rather than distinctions.

title: Hourly Wages in Crowdworking: A Meta-Analysis
abstract: This development has led to increasing interest in the wages people earn on crowdworking platforms. This study extends the literature, which is often based on a single platform or region, through a meta-analysis of prevalent hourly wages. After a systematic literature search, the paper considers 22 primary empirical studies. Microtasks result in an hourly wage of less than $6. Researchers should be aware that remuneration and work processes can systematically affect the data.

title: Component of Trust for Developing Crowdwork System: A Systematic Literature Review
abstract: Crowdwork is a system that brings job providers and crowdworkers into a portal. New problems arise in the crowdwork system; trust is one of the main issues. This research aims to examine the components that affect trust in a crowdwork system, using systematic literature review. This research produces 11 components and 38 indicators, so stakeholders can be aware of how to increase trust.
venue: Advances in Science, Technology and Engineering Systems

title: Algorithmic Management in the Future of Work: A Systematic Literature Review in the Context of Gig Workers
abstract: Algorithmic management has become a dominant managerial mechanism in gig work, yet its implications for workers remain fragmented in the literature. This study aims to systematically examine and synthesize prior research by identifying core mechanisms, benefits, challenges, and unresolved research gaps. A PRISMA-guided SLR of 34 studies. The originality lies in extending the traditional IPO framework into an IPOO model to capture long-term consequences.

title: Gig Workers Under Algorithmic Management: A Systematic Literature Review And Theoretical Synthesis
abstract: Scholarly interest in gig work has intensified since 2020. However, existing scholarship remains theoretically dispersed and methodologically uneven, limiting cumulative knowledge development. Addressing this gap, the study undertakes a systematic literature review guided by PRISMA-informed protocols. By synthesizing work through Job Demands-Resources, Self-Determination and Institutional theory, it advances a theory-integrative framework and a future research agenda.

title: Algorithmic management and app-work in the gig economy: A research agenda for employment relations and HRM
abstract: Current understanding of what constitutes work in the growing gig economy is heavily conflated, ranging from conceptualisations of independent contracting to other forms of contingent labour. This article calls for a move away from problematic aggregations by proposing a classification of gig work into three variants. Focusing on app-work, it proposes new lines of enquiry and a series of research questions to guide future research.

title: Algorithmic management in the global gig economy: an interdisciplinary systematic literature review and critical discourse analysis
abstract: This article presents a systematic literature review of 103 sources, complemented by critical discourse analysis. While gig work engages millions worldwide, scholarly attention has centered disproportionately on Western contexts. The CDA uncovers how academic narratives often oscillate between portraying algorithmic management as digital Taylorism and a catalyst for worker autonomy. The review highlights a critical gap in global and comparative analysis.

title: Algorithmic Management in Organizations? From Edge Case to Center Stage
abstract: This article offers a comprehensive review of the literature on algorithmic management from HRM, organizational psychology and OB. AM creates a gray zone in which workers exist in an ambiguous space, neither fully inside nor outside organizational boundaries. This poses a unique challenge for scholars, whose frameworks typically rely on clear distinctions between employment and freelancing, often overlooking the complexities of this gray zone. It proposes an agenda for future research.
venue: Annual Review of Org. Psychology and OB

title: Algorithmic Surveillance and Psychological Safety in the Gig Economy: A Bibliometric and Systematic Literature Review
abstract: This review investigates the intersections of algorithmic surveillance, algorithmic management and psychological safety. Using PRISMA 2020, a Scopus corpus of 242 articles and VOSviewer. Findings show exponential growth in publications. Four thematic clusters emerged. The review develops an integrated conceptual model and provides ten research gaps and a structured future agenda.

title: Algorithmic management in a work context
abstract: Exploring algorithmic management as a sociotechnical concept, we discuss how it may influence existing power and social structures within organizations. We identify three key issues: how AM shapes pre-existing power dynamics; how it demands new roles while fostering oppositional attitudes; and how it impacts knowledge and information exchange, unpacking opacity. We conclude by situating this piece in broader discussions on the future of work and identifying future research steps.

title: Control or Empowerment: Toward a Research Agenda on the Duality of Algorithmic Management
abstract: Despite a growing body of research on algorithmic management, the field lacks tools to capture worker experiences, hindering empirical investigations. This study introduces the Perceived Algorithmic Management Questionnaire to confirm the concept of algorithmic management duality. Drawing on job demands-resources theory, we argue the four dimensions both constrain and enable engagement, setting the stage for further exploration.

title: Research on the rights protection mechanism of gig workers under algorithmic management based on Citespace
abstract: Using quantitative analysis and the CiteSpace literature analysis tool, this paper conducts a visual analysis of relevant international literature from 2015 to 2025 to explore the research status, hot issues and trends of the protection of gig workers' rights under algorithm management. Research hotspots have shifted to multi-dimensional social equity. Existing research still has shortcomings in algorithm transparency and legal framework.
